evals.expected_output: Scores the POC-kickoff call against every dimension in references/rubric.md (success criteria defined and agreed, technical scope agreed, stakeholders identified and committed, POC timeline and exit criteria set, resourcing confirmed). Every dimension gets a Status (Covered/Partial/Missed/Unclear) and, for anything not fully covered, a one-line Note. Every finding is backed by a direct quote or timestamp from the transcript — no unsourced findings. Closes with a go/no-go/needs-one-more-call read and the dimension(s) that decided it.
expectations: Every dimension in the rubric gets a Status
Every finding cites a quote or timestamp from the transcript, or is marked Unclear rather than guessed
No finding is asserted without evidence
Closes with a single go/no-go/needs-one-more-call read naming the deciding dimension(s)
Cites at least one specific, concrete detail from the transcript (a number, name, or quoted phrase) rather than a generic paraphrase that could apply to any call
evals.name: qualify-to-poc-eval-1

evals.prompt: run qualify-to-poc on a transcript of a kickoff call that, by any reasonable read, locked down success criteria, scope, stakeholders, timeline, and resourcing thoroughly and left little unaddressed
evals.expected_output: The audit does not come back mostly Missed/Partial just because the rubric has multiple dimensions. The rubric.md 'reads-well-too' check is applied before finalizing: if a clearly well-run kickoff still reads as mostly gaps, the evidence bar is loosened rather than reported as-is.
expectations: A genuinely well-run kickoff call is not scored as mostly Missed
The reads-well-too check from references/rubric.md is applied before the audit is finalized
evals.name: qualify-to-poc-eval-2

evals.expected_output: Treats this as a structural hygiene sweep, not a call-quality audit, and says so explicitly. Checks each deal row entering or in pilot/POC stage for whether fields corresponding to the rubric's dimensions (success criteria, technical scope, stakeholders, timeline/exit criteria, resourcing) are present and non-trivial. Outputs a table sorted by deal value descending so the highest-value gaps surface first. Makes no claim about what was actually said on any call.
expectations: States explicitly that CSV mode is a structural check, not a call-quality claim
Output is sorted by deal value descending
Does not claim to know what happened on any specific call from CRM fields alone
evals.name: qualify-to-poc-eval-3
